turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Afternoon, Mr Naidoo, come and sit. Shame, it's baking out there today, hey?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, Doctor. Thank you. Yes, it is uncomfortably warm. We sat at the robot by the garage for a good while.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The N1 was at a standstill, Doctor. And he had the cricket on the whole way, volume up.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): The test in Cape Town? I caught some of the lunch session. The captain looked properly settled.

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): He did, until that catch at slip just before tea. I do apologise, I follow it rather closely. My late wife's brother played club cricket in Durban, so the radio stays on.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He had it so loud I missed the turnoff at Malibongwe. Then we spent ten minutes on whether the opener should have reviewed the lbw.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I still say it was missing leg. Anyway, they say this heat breaks by Thursday, which will be a mercy.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd have reviewed it, for what it's worth. Lovely, let's leave the cricket and the weather, and talk about how you've been keeping.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course, Doctor. I am sorry to have wandered.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): So what's been troubling you lately?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): It is the cough, Doctor, every morning, and I become rather short of breath when I walk any distance.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about that cough. How long has it been going on?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, years, if I am honest. A smoker's cough, I suppose. But these past three weeks it has been distinctly worse, ever since the chest infection.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the shortness of breath, when did you first notice that?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): The phlegm in the morning is pale now, not green. I bring up a small amount before breakfast, and then it eases off.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so pale phlegm in the mornings. Coming back to the breathlessness, how long has that been a problem?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, about two months, Doctor. On the flat I cope well enough, but the stairs up to the flat leave me quite puffed, and I have to stop halfway.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He holds the rail and stops halfway. I stay with him during the week, so I see it most days.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain when that happens?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. No pain at all.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you coughed up any blood, or woken in the night gasping for air?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood, thankfully. And I sleep through, apart from the odd cough at dawn.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss, or fevers since that infection cleared?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No weight loss. The fever settled once I finished the antibiotics. That was last Tuesday.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): What antibiotic did they give you?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Amoxicillin. Five hundred milligrams, three times a day, for five days. The clinic doctor prescribed it for the chest infection.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): And which inhalers are you using at the moment?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): The blue one, salbutamol, two puffs when I need it. And the brown preventer, beclomethasone, two puffs of two hundred micrograms, twice a day. That is what they told me to do.

[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Supposed to, yes. The brown one lives on the bedside table. He skips it some days, especially if he's late for work. I'd say he gets to it about half the time, if that.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you still smoke?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I do, I am afraid. About ten a day... well, actually, maybe twenty. It varies with the day. I have smoked since I was twenty-one, and I turned sixty-eight in March.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you on any other tablets? Something for blood pressure, for instance?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing for blood pressure. Only atorvastatin, twenty milligrams at night, for my cholesterol. I have taken that for years.

[SEG0034] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry to come in, Doctor. Spirometry from just now: FEV1 is 1.7 litres, 61 percent predicted, FVC is 3.4 litres, 89 percent predicted, and the ratio is 50 percent. On air his saturation is 94 percent, pulse 86, respiratory rate 20.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thanks, Sister. Mr Naidoo, that shows the airflow is quite reduced. My working impression is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from the smoking, but I'll keep that provisional until the full printout is filed.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): With the infection, about three weeks back, he was feverish and the phlegm was green for about a week. Then the amoxicillin, and he's been off it since Tuesday.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): That infection does sound as if it has settled. Do you have any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of, Doctor.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd like the brown inhaler used properly, please, two puffs of the two hundred microgram one, twice a day, every day, not only when you remember. The blue one stays two puffs as you need it, for the breathlessness.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall try to be more regular with it. I do apologise for being careless.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): No apology needed. About the cigarettes, would you like some help to stop? I can refer you to our stop-smoking service.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, please do. I think it is time. I am a little nervous about it, but I would like the support.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll ask reception to book that. And if the breathlessness is no better in six weeks, come back and see me. Sooner, obviously, if you cough up blood, or the fever returns, or you can't finish a sentence.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. Thank you, Doctor.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll move the brown inhaler to beside his toothbrush, morning and night. And I won't buy the cigarettes when I do the shopping.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): That would be a real help, thank you. Sister, is the blood pressure in the folder as well?
[SEG0047] person_4 (NURSE): Yes, Doctor. Earlier it was one thirty-six over eighty-two. Nothing else outstanding.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Mr Naidoo, use those inhalers as we've said, go along to the quit session, and come back if you're not easier in six weeks, or earlier if you worsen.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you very much for your time, Doctor. Good afternoon.
